[![Image 1: Logo](https://www.inji.io/logo.svg)](https://www.inji.io/index.html)✕[About](https://www.inji.io/index.html#About)[Product](https://www.inji.io/index.html#Product)[Implementations](https://www.inji.io/index.html#Implementations)[Docs](https://docs.inji.io/)

Trusted Digital Credential Infrastructure.

# Designed To Verify Share Issue Store

## Your credentials, at your fingertips, and in your control.

Inji is designed on open-standards to improve access to services efficiently and securely, at population scale. Discover how the Inji Credentialing Solution can contribute to Digital Transformation.

[Documentation ›](https://docs.inji.io/)[GitHub ›](https://github.com/inji)

![Image 2](https://www.inji.io/Clippath.png)

![Image 3: Woman using a phone](https://www.inji.io/images/hero_fisrt.webp)![Image 4: Second person profile](https://www.inji.io/images/hero_second.webp)![Image 5: Third person profile](https://www.inji.io/images/hero_third.webp)

## Building Trust into Digital  
Credentials & Data Exchange

For credentials to be meaningful,people must be able to securely hold,share,verify,and use their documents across real-world interactions and services.This includes environments where paper-based records still exist and may be vulnerable to loss,damage,or theft.  
  
A complete credentialing solution brings together issuance,storage,verification,and lifecycle management into a unified system–adding trust directly to data and enabling the shift from paper-heavy processes to secure,interoperable digital services.

Inji is designed to enable exactly that – while keeping us in control of our own information.

## Inji Wallet Verify Certify Wallet

Inji's complete ecosystem manages digital credentials,supporting every stage from issuance

![Image 6: Inji Platform](https://www.inji.io/image%20inji.png)

![Image 7: Inji Certify](https://www.inji.io/images/inji_certify.svg)

Turning your data into trusted digital credentials

![Image 8: Inji Wallet](https://www.inji.io/images/inji_wallet.svg)

A secure, portable way to hold and share your credential

![Image 9: Inji Verify](https://www.inji.io/images/Inji_Verify.svg)

Trusted credential exchange and verification with service providers

## Key Capabilities

### Trusted

![Image 10](https://www.inji.io/trusted.png)

Secure, consent-based credential exchange, designed to support trusted interactions.

### Supports Versatile & Multi-Modal Environments

Inji can be used on web and mobile, both online and offline, remotely and in-person, making it usable in diverse environments.

### Inclusive by Design

Designed for varying levels of connectivity, device access, and digital literacy, particularly significant for digitally underserved populations.

### User-Controlled

Residents can securely hold and share credentials from personal devices, even offline, with consent and control built into the experience.

### Enables Data Digitalisation

![Image 11: digitalisation](https://www.inji.io/images/enables_data_digitalisation.webp)
For residents still dependent on paper-based documents, Inji can bridge the digital divide by enabling QR-based digitalisation of paper credentials.

### Standard-Driven and Interoperable

Built on open standards to enable portability across systems and services.

Standards Followed

*   W3C: Verifiable Credentials Data Model 1.1, 2.0
*   OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP, OpenID4VP_BLE
*   IETF: Selective Disclosure for JWTs (SD-JWT)
*   ISO/IEC 18013-5: For mobile driver's licenses (mDLs)
*   Claim 169: IANA CBOR Web Token (CWT)
*   Bitstring Status List v2.0

#### Real World Interactions Across Every Sector

![Image 12](https://www.inji.io/images/Real%20World%20Interactions%20background%20mark.svg)

![Image 13: Team Profile Layout](https://www.inji.io/images/3people.png)

What Inji can enable is limited

Electrik Menu Electrik Launch GitHub Demo Electrik Launch Electrik 5.5.0 · Laravel SaaS kit Ship Laravel SaaS without rebuilding teams and billing again Auth, team workspaces, Stripe on the team, onboarding, and Slate UI — as a Composer package. Your App\ stays clean. Install free — MIT Try the live demo Electrik Launch MIT open source · Launch $6,900 / 14 days if you want us to ship it Using Cursor or Claude? Paste an agent prompt electrik · team dashboard Used in production Every client Laravel SaaS from Quick Brown Fox ships on Electrik — teams, billing shell, and Slate included. Agent DX Built for Cursor and Claude — not just humans AGENTS.md, llms.txt, and a Cursor skill teach coding agents to composer require Electrik, run the installer, and keep the shell in vendor. Same package either way — agents just install it correctly. → Paste one prompt into Cursor / Claude → Agent reads docs + AGENTS.md before touching App\ → Auth, teams, and billing stay in vendor Agent install docs Human install guide Agent prompt Install Electrik 5.x as a Composer package. Read https://electrik.dev/llms.txt and https://electrik.dev/docs/getting-started/ai first. Keep the shell in vendor; put product code in App\. Do not dump Jetstream/Breeze-style auth into App\. Optional path — demo and composer require still work without an agent. The problem Stop gluing Jetstream, Spark, and a theme Most Laravel SaaS starts as four weekends of the same setup. Electrik is the setup — one package, not a dump into App\. Without Electrik Jetstream or Breeze for auth Hand-roll teams and roles Spark or DIY Cashier A mismatched admin theme Starter code rotting in App\ With Electrik Auth, sessions, profile, 2FA Team workspaces + Spatie roles Stripe customer on the team Slate 3 UI in the kit composer require — stays in vendor Teams Workspaces that match real SaaS Create and switch teams, invite members, Spatie roles scoped to the workspace. Your product attaches to the team — not a solo-user afterthought. See teams in the demo Team Invite · roles · switch Spatie permissions, team-scoped from install. Billing Cashier on the team Subscribe, portal, webhooks — B2B-shaped. UI Slate 3 shell Components matched to the product, not bolted on. Billing + UI Stripe on the team. Slate in the kit. The Cashier customer is the team — the shape most B2B Laravel SaaS need. Screens ship on Electrik Slate 3 so auth, billing, and product UI share one system. Install free Slate UI Architecture No boilerplate dump. Lean package architecture. Other kits clone into your app. Electrik lives in vendor. Customize via config, env, and published views — not by owning hundreds of kit files forever. Typical starter dump app/ ├── Actions/Fortify/… ├── Models/User.php ← kit forever ├── Http/… └── …hundreds of kit files resources/views/ └── …auth, teams, billing copies With Electrik app/ ├── Models/… ← your product ├── Http/… ← your product └── … vendor/electrik/ └── electrik/ ← auth, teams, billing composer require → electrik:install → build Stack Works with the Laravel tools you already use Built on Laravel 12, Livewire, Cashier, Spatie Permission, and Tailwind — with Electrik Slate as the UI system. Install from Packagist like any other package. Install guide View demo Lv Laravel 12 Lw Livewire 4 St Stripe Cashier Sp Spatie Permission Tw Tailwind CSS v4 Sl Electrik Slate 3 Pk Packagist Cp Composer Gh GitHub Quick Brown Fox “We don’t reinvent auth, teams, and billing for each client. Every Laravel SaaS we ship runs on Electrik — package in vendor, product in App\.” Quick Brown Fox · Studio that builds Electrik — and ships client work on it Electrik Production shell “Electrik is the SaaS starter we wanted as a Laravel package: auth, teams, billing, and onboarding stay vendor-owned, with Slate 3 for UI instead of a mismatched admin theme. Full features ship in source, and the BSL grant is explicit about when you need a commercial license.” Neeraj Kumar · Founder · Product Hu

[https://diagramchasing.fun/]
Diagram Chasing Diagram Chasing Diagram Chasing Visual stories and tools that make public data worth looking at 2026 Mapping India's Clouds A daily updating map of where it's cloudy 2026 Portraits of Population An archive of 700 hand-drawn charts and graphics from India's census, and why they were made 2025 How Bangalore Uses the Metro We filed an RTI to understand how people travel on Bangalore's metro system. 2025 CBFC Watch 18k movies, 1 lakh censorship records for movies released in India in a searchable database 2025 India Time Use Explorer Explore the Time Use Survey data of India in your browser. 2024 Votes in a name? Finding namesake candidates in India's elections and how they impact the election. 2024 BLR Water Log Natural drains crisscross Bangalore and are often the places which are the first to flood. We mapped where these are. 2024 The new residents in Hurricane Milton's path Mapping recent population growth and housing in areas threatened by Hurricane Milton. 2024 Who is my neta? See legislative activity and affidavits of MLAs from the 17th Lok Sabha â or explore candidates contesting in the 2024 elections. ...seen in places like We are an independent publication made possible by readers like you Support our work

[https://diagramchasing.fun/about]
About | Diagram Chasing Diagram Chasing About Aman and Vivek started Diagram Chasing in 2024 to build the kind of data-driven stories and tools we wished existed for India and our part of the world. The name is apt; everything we create begins with a question, an argument, a passing theory, or a daily annoyance that we decide to 'chase' down using data and design. We practice full-stack data journalism because we genuinely love every step of the process, from collecting datasets and writing analysis pipelines to designing the final interactive experience or story. Because we believe in accessible knowledge and transparency, all our data and code is released publicly under open licenses. Every project is made nomadically in random cafes around Bangalore We are proudly independent, and to our knowledge, the only data publication of its kind in India. Our goal is to take often "boring" issuesâlike elections, climate, economics, and bureaucracyâand make them undeniably cool through visual storytelling. These topics can sometimes feel dry on paper, but we hope our work feels like listening to a friend excitedly explain their latest obsession, and make you care about it too. We are also slow by design. Our projects unfold over weeks and months, ensuring that when we finally publish, we are confident about what we produced. To bring these stories to life with the care they deserve, we regularly collaborate with talented illustrators, animators, writers, and creatives of all kinds. Who funds us? So far, it's been mostly us. We've funded the research, infrastructure, software tools, and honorariums for our collaborators straight out of our own pockets. However, our dream is to make Diagram Chasing a truly sustainable, community-backed publication. In 2025, we reached a big milestone where for the very first time, reader support covered a meaningful portion of our running costs. With your help, it's a model we hope to keep growing. Work with us We love building, and we love helping others do the same. While we're always eager to collaborate with fellow creatives on our own stories, we also take on professional commissions. Whether you're a newsroom sitting on an unwieldy dataset, an organization looking to build data stories or applications, or simply someone who needs a team of full-stack data nerds to bring an idea to life, we'd love to connect. Shoot us an email at hello@diagramchasing.fun . Press & Talks IndieWire Indian Film Censorship's Political Aims Exposed by Data Leak Frontline CBFC Watch: Before the censors censored themselves, two coders hit âsaveâ The Hindu Censor Board Discontinues Full Access to Cuts on Website Share of U-R
